newsitem.title: CANADA: Martin says Canada on track to meet program cuts.
newsitem.headline: Martin says Canada on track to meet program cuts.

text.p: The federal government is on track to meet cuts in program spending as set out in the 1995 budget, Finance Minister Paul Martin and Treasury Board President Marcel Masse said on Thursday.
"The government has bettered its deficit targets for three consecutive years and reductions to government program spending will be delivered on time and on target," they said in a statement.

The statement said departmental spending subject to Program Review -- that process by which the Liberal government slashed nearly every department's programs in an effort to bring down the overall budget deficit -- would fall to C$44.99 billion in 1997-98 from C$51.72 billion in 1994-95.
In fact, Martin's budget in February 1995 had forecast that that would fall to C$42.09 billion in 1997-98.

"The difference between the 1995 budget and the current number is largely explained by the C$1.4 billion in new spending initiatives announced over the past two years and C$820 million in framework adjustments," the statement said.
"This leaves a residual amount of C$655 million which, based on recent experience, could be more than off-set by the 'lapse' in departmental spending," the statement continued.

Delineating the C$1.42 billion in new spending, it listed C$425 million for infrastructure, C$145 million for jobs and youth, C$228 million for national revenue enforcement and C$141 million for anti-smuggling initiative/firearms.
Overall departmental spending is planned to decline to C$50.23 billion in 1997-98 -- the year starts April 1 -- from C$55.86 billion in 1994-95.

The statement subtracts from that figure spending not subject to Program Review -- spending that is supposed to rise to C$5.24 billion in 1997-98 from C$4.14 billion in 1994-95 -- in order to arrive at the spending subject to Program Review.
"By bettering its deficit targets over the past the past three years the government has been able to invest in key priority areas for Canadians," the statement said.

"The 1995-96 deficit target of C$28.6 billion was bettered by C$4.1 billion, which included C$800 million in spending initiatives. The 1996-97 deficit will not be any higher than C$19.0 billion -- C$5.3 billion lower than the original deficit target of C$24.3 billion. The 1997 budget included C$1.0 billion in spending initiatives for 1997-98."
